title: A bounded rational solution of the homogeneous edge system yields a linearly ordered colouring with two plus log-two of the dynamic range many colours
author: Johan H{\aa}stad, Bj\"orn Martinsson, Tamio-Vesa Nakajima, Stanislav \v{Z}ivn\'y
authors: Johan H{\aa}stad, Bj\"orn Martinsson, Tamio-Vesa Nakajima, Stanislav \v{Z}ivn\'y
work: A logarithmic approximation of linearly ordered colourings
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the dyadic colouring lemma of the paper (author lemma at source lines 266-271, label lemma:unbal): any solution u of the homogeneous system Av = 0^m whose coordinates have maximal absolute value M and minimal absolute value m > 0 yields an LO colouring with 2 + log_2(M/m) colours. The proof (source lines 273-288) constructs the colouring rather than citing one: it first reduces to the equivalent requirement that the minimum colour in each edge be unique by reversing the colour order, then assigns even colours to coordinates in dyadic positive windows and odd colours to coordinates in dyadic negative windows (proof lines 276-281), and verifies the unique-minimum property by showing that two vertices of an edge sharing a colour force the third coordinate below the corresponding dyadic threshold, whence its colour is strictly smaller (proof lines 283-288). The point of the lemma is the logarithmic dependence on the ratio M/m, which is what lets the algorithm of that section spend few colours. H2.
